title: Shift normalization of canonical ringed-slice comparisons
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be continuous and define a morphism $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ whose inverse image preserves finite limits. Let $R$ on $\mathcal D$ and $S$ on $\mathcal C$ be sheaves of commutative rings with a specified isomorphism $f^{-1}R\cong S$. For $V\in\mathcal D$ put $U=u(V)$, use the restricted rings on the slice sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and let $f_V$ be the induced ringed morphism [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\beta_E:j_V^*Rf_*E\cong R(f_V)_*j_U^*E$ and $\theta_P:Lf_V^*j_V^*P\cong j_U^*Lf^*P$ be the canonical, derived-adjunction-compatible comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization], and let $\tau_{M,N}:j_V^*(M\otimes_R^LN)\cong j_V^*M\otimes_{R|_V}^Lj_V^*N$ be the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]; also use the corresponding tensor comparison for $j_U^*$. Then $\beta$, $\theta$, and both tensor comparisons commute with the canonical integer-shift isomorphisms in each input. Precisely, for each comparison $c:F\cong G$ and each input shifted by $n\in\mathbf Z$, $s_G c_{[n]}=c[n]s_F$, with the other inputs fixed. The unary shift is $(K[n])^r=K^{r+n}$ with differential $(-1)^nd_K$. For the total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the shift map $A[n]\otimes B\cong(A\otimes B)[n]$ is identity on summands and $A\otimes B[n]\cong(A\otimes B)[n]$ multiplies the summand of first degree $p$ by $(-1)^{np}$. The derived pullback and pushforward shifts are those obtained by shifting their resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift].

source.place: Tag 08FI, lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open, and the preceding exact-restriction discussion; Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, representative construction. Signed-shift comparison is an agent-written calculation from these constructions, not a verbatim Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Write $r=j_V^*$ and $t=j_U^*$. On complexes restriction commutes with every integer shift by the identity: on $T\to V$ both $r(K[n])^a$ and $(rK)[n]^a$ are $K^{a+n}(T)$, and both differentials are $(-1)^n d_K$. The same holds for $t$. Use these comparisons for the exact derived restrictions. For tensor shifts use the chain isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], with the precise unsigned first-input and $(-1)^{np}$ second-input formulas in the statement. Shifts preserve flat-term K-flat representatives: flatness of the terms is unchanged by reindexing, and for every acyclic $Z$ the signed tensor isomorphism identifies $Z\otimes P[n]$ with $(Z\otimes P)[n]$, which is acyclic since its cohomology in degree $a$ is that of $Z\otimes P$ in degree $a+n$.

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution $E\to I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Restriction $tI$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Thus the two sides of $\beta_E$ are represented by $r f_*I$ and $(f_V)_*tI$. The canonical comparison is the image of the termwise comparison: this is exactly the right-derived-unit normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-derived-comparisons]. By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], at $T\to V$ it is the identity on $I^a(uT)$ with its $R(T)$-action. For $E[n]$ choose $I[n]$; this is a valid resolution by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift], and its restriction is $tI[n]$. In degree $a$, both routes in the shift square for $\beta$ are the identity on $I^{a+n}(uT)$; all differentials are $(-1)^n d_I$. Applying localization proves $s_G\beta_{E[n]}=\beta_E[n]s_F$. These are the specified resolution shifts by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. Naturality carries the identity along $E\simeq QI$, so it holds for every unbounded $E$.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0D6G (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); signed-shift equations expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Put $L=Lf^*$, $R=Rf_*$, $L'=Lf_V^*$ and $R'=R(f_V)_*$. Let $\eta$ and $\eta'$ denote the two units. Adjunction compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-slice-localization] says that $\theta_P:L'rP\to tLP$ has adjunct $h_P=\beta_{LP}\circ r(\eta_P):rP\to R'tLP$, equivalently $\theta_P=\varepsilon'_{tLP}\circ L'(h_P)$. Write $a_P:L(P[n])\to LP[n]$, $b_E:R(E[n])\to RE[n]$ and $a',b'$ for the local resolution shifts. The unit equations of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift], globally and locally, have exactly the normalization specified in [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique]. For $B=tLP$ they give, using Step 2 and naturality of $\beta$ at $a_P$, $$b'_B\circ R'(t a_P)\circ h_{P[n]}=h_P[n].$$ Indeed the left side is $b'_B R'(t a_P)\beta_{L(P[n])}r\eta_{P[n]}=b'_B\beta_{LP[n]}rR(a_P)r\eta_{P[n]}=\beta_{LP}[n]r(b_{LP}R(a_P)\eta_{P[n]})=\beta_{LP}[n]r(\eta_P[n])$. Restriction-shift identities from Step 1 are suppressed in this formula.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0D6G (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); signed-shift equations expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Take adjuncts under $L'\dashv R'$ of the two arrows $L'(rP[n])\to B[n]$ given by $t(a_P)\circ\theta_{P[n]}$ and $\theta_P[n]\circ a'_{rP}$. The first adjunct is $R'(t a_P)\circ h_{P[n]}$. The second is $(b'_B)^{-1}\circ h_P[n]$: expand its adjunct as $R'(\theta_P[n])R'(a'_{rP})\eta'_{rP[n]}$, replace $R'(a'_{rP})\eta'_{rP[n]}$ by $(b'_{L'rP})^{-1}\eta'_{rP}[n]$ using the local unit equation, and use naturality of $b'$ at $\theta_P$. Step 3 says these adjuncts agree. The adjunction bijection therefore gives $t(a_P)\theta_{P[n]}=\theta_P[n]a'_{rP}$, which is precisely the requested shift equation for $\theta$ after inserting the restriction comparisons of Step 1. This argument fixes the comparison by its unit equation, so it applies to the specified canonical $\theta$, including the inverse orientation used when stating the slice-localization isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0D6G (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); signed-shift equations expanded by the agent.

proof.text: Let $j_W^*$ be either restriction ($W=V$ on $\mathcal D$, or $W=U$ on $\mathcal C$). Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $A,B$ for its two derived inputs by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The tensor normalization in the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose] applies to this arbitrary small ringed site: $j_W^*A,j_W^*B$ are valid flat-term K-flat representatives, and the canonical derived tensor comparison is represented by the chain isomorphism $j_W^*\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes B)\to\operatorname{Tot}(j_W^*A\otimes j_W^*B)$ whose $(p,q)$ summand is $\mu_{A^p,B^q}$, the restriction tensor isomorphism sending local $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$. Step 1 allows $A[n],B[n]$ as the representatives of the shifted inputs. Thus all four tensor shift squares can be computed on precisely these representatives, with no new choices of tensor or comparison.

source.place: Tags 08FI (lemma-restrict-K-injective-to-open), 0D6G (lemma-restrict-direct-image-open), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); signed-shift equations expanded by the agent.

proof.text: On a summand of first degree $p$ in $A[n]\otimes B$, the two routes around the first-input square both give $\mu_{A^{p+n},B^q}$ with coefficient $1$, merely reindexing the total degree by $n$. On a summand $A^p\otimes B^{q+n}$ in $A\otimes B[n]$, both routes around the second-input square give $(-1)^{np}\mu_{A^p,B^{q+n}}$: applying restriction or the module isomorphism $\mu$ commutes with multiplication by $(-1)^{np}$. These are equal chain maps, since the signed maps of [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts] are chain maps for the differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Their images in the derived category agree. The representative-model isomorphisms and the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extend this equality from flat-term K-flat pairs to all derived pairs. Applying the calculation once with $W=V$ and once with $W=U$ proves the tensor assertions for every integer $n$, with the other input fixed. Together with Steps 2 and 4 this proves all the stated shift equations.
